---
title: "Week 5 — Building Interactive Apps with Streamlit"
---

> From notebook to application. This module is the hinge of the course: students learn to turn analyses into interactive Streamlit apps, the delivery format used for both projects and all later modules.

## 📖 Background & Motivation

A notebook is a great place to *develop* a visualization, but a poor place to *deliver* one to someone who isn't a programmer. Streamlit closes that gap: with a few lines of pure Python, a script becomes an interactive web app with widgets, layout, and live-updating charts. For a data-science course, this is more than convenience — it is the difference between a static figure and a tool someone can explore.

This week is deliberately tooling-heavy. We cover Streamlit's execution model (the script re-runs top-to-bottom on every interaction), the widget set, layout primitives (columns, tabs, sidebar), and — crucially — caching, which is what keeps an app responsive when it loads data or fits a model. We also deploy a first app to the web. Everything after this week assumes Streamlit fluency: the modality modules end in small apps, and the final project is a deployed client–server Streamlit application. Getting comfortable now is what makes the client–server weeks (11–13) feasible in a single session.

---

## 🔎 Learning Objectives

- Explain Streamlit's re-run execution model and use `st.session_state` and caching appropriately.
- Build apps with widgets, layout (columns/tabs/sidebar), and live charts.
- Convert an existing notebook analysis into an interactive app.
- Deploy a Streamlit app to the web.

## 🧭 Session Outline (2.5 hours)

> Single 2.5-hour block, 6:10-8:40 PM. Tooling week — hands-on dominates.

### Block 1 — Concepts & Theory (~25 min, PowerPoint)

1. Why apps, not just notebooks: delivery and exploration (6 min)
2. The re-run model: how Streamlit executes, and why caching matters (13 min)
3. Layout and state: columns, tabs, sidebar, `session_state` (6 min)

### Block 2 — Guided Demonstration (~45 min, live coding)

1. Build an app with a sidebar, widgets, and a live chart (19 min)
2. Add caching to a slow data load; see the speedup (13 min)
3. Push to GitHub and deploy to Streamlit Community Cloud (13 min)

### ☕ Break (~15 min)

### Block 3 — Hands-On Activity (~55 min, students working)

1. Each student takes a notebook from Weeks 2–4 and converts it to an app (31 min)
2. Add at least two widgets and a layout element (12 min)
3. Deploy it and share the URL (12 min)

### Block 4 — Wrap-Up & Homework Preview (~10 min)

1. Walk through a few deployed apps (6 min)
2. Preview homework and the mid-term project (4 min)

## 💻 Notebook / App Snippets

### App skeleton with widgets and layout

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st
import seaborn as sns

st.title("Penguins Explorer")
species = st.sidebar.multiselect("Species", ["Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"],
                                 default=["Adelie"])
df = sns.load_dataset("penguins").dropna()
df = df[df["species"].isin(species)]

col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
col1.metric("Rows", len(df))
col2.metric("Avg mass (g)", round(df["body_mass_g"].mean(), 1))
st.scatter_chart(df, x="flipper_length_mm", y="body_mass_g", color="species")
```

### Caching a slow load

```python
import streamlit as st, pandas as pd

@st.cache_data
def load_data(path):
    return pd.read_csv(path)   # only runs once per unique path

df = load_data("big_file.csv")
```

### Session state (remember across re-runs)

```python
import streamlit as st
if "count" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.count = 0
if st.button("Increment"):
    st.session_state.count += 1
st.write(st.session_state.count)
```

## 🏠 Homework

1. Take an analysis from Weeks 2–4 and turn it into a deployed Streamlit app.
2. Include at least: a sidebar, two widgets, a layout element (columns or tabs), and caching.
3. Deploy it and submit the live URL plus the repo link to Blackboard.

**Rubric (10 pts)**

- App runs and is deployed (3)
- Effective widgets and layout (3)
- Correct use of caching / state (2)
- Clarity and usefulness of the app (2)
